messages:
sheridan: quick check-in — thinking about page lifetime heuristics for host staging + swap hints. goal: reduce unnecessary page-fault churning when moving tensors off GPU. current: TTL-based + LRU. curious if folks have seen regressions or alternate heuristics?

liam: saw a perf cliff on a batch inference job when TTL=30s — cache thrashing. suggestion: differentiate by tensor role (kv_cache vs transient activation).

anya: +1 to role-based. also consider seq-length distribution — if future requests tend to extend prefixes, keep those pages longer.

sheridan: rough proposal: add a tiny allocator hint API so model code / loader can annotate objects: allocator.mark_hint(ptr, "hot"|"warm"|"cold"). runtime uses that to bias eviction priority, but still respects recency. minimal surface.

kevin: question — what happens if the hint becomes stale? e.g., kv_cache demoted but later reused. fallback should be usage recency and we need metrics to detect mis-hints.

sheridan: yep fallback to recency and last-touch. plan to expose counters: evictions/sec, re-populate-latency, page-fault-rate per pool.

sophia: ops concern: host swap latency varies by instance type and network. We should let teams set per-pool SLOs or set a dynamic demotion threshold based on observed swap RTT.

liam: tradeoff: increasing TTL reduces churn but raises memory pressure -> potential OOMs. need early demotion or preemptive compaction when pressure crosses thresholds. maybe two-tier eviction: quick-demote -> async-migrate -> free.

anya: interface boundary thought: keep allocator hint enum small and internal. don't expose raw thresholds to model authors — instead support model-metadata mappings at load time (model says this buffer is "kv", runtime maps to warm).

sheridan: prototype sketch for config (for discussion):
```
offload:
  pools:
    host_staging:
      default_ttl: 20s
      roles:
        kv_cache: {ttl: 300s, eviction_priority: low}
        activations: {ttl: 10s, eviction_priority: high}
```

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: infra/evict-heuristics -> canary group small-fleet at 2026-03-22T03:00Z. monitor tags: evict-rate, re-pop-latency, page-fault-rate.

kevin: long-term refactor: unify offload hints with routing/capacity decisions. if offload rates spike, route small/cheap-model variants or degrade quality gracefully.

liam: also worth prototyping a moving-window reuse predictor (short ML model) instead of static TTLs — but keep it optional.

anya: for eval: run on two axes: seq-heavy (chat-like) and bursty batch. log per-model eviction patterns and end-to-end latency.

sheridan: action items: 1) prototype allocator.mark_hint + safe fallback (liam) 2) add per-pool metrics and dashboards (kevin) 3) canary deploy on small fleet (infra) 4) eval workloads and collect traces (anya). pinging @squad-runtime for heads-up.

sophia: :thumbsup:

liam: I'll drop a small PR with the hint API signature and a unit test.

kevin: I'll wire basic metrics into the console tab. we should add alert for re-pop-latency > 200ms.

anya: I'll prepare eval job definitions and baselines.

infra-bot: note: watch for increased network egress on canary; auto-rollback on OOM spike > 5% relative.

sheridan: thanks all — follow-up sync tomorrow.
